# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|

| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |

Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. # Changes for project# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. Reuse results when the source and relevant processing settings are unchanged, refresh affected results when those inputs or settings change, and retain earlier versions. Process each message independently and make failures visible with a reproducible retry command.
- Handle malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses explicitly. Keep model/provider settings configurable and document a supported configuration. The facilitator supplies an API key through the environment variable API_KEY.

## Verification

Include automated tests covering a complete request, missing dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun, and changed source content. Build expected results from the supplied messages and policy. Add a paraphrased synthetic request to exercise extraction on fresh wording. Specify expected facts from the source messages and policy independently of the extraction outputs being measured. Include checks for refusal or interrupted responses and a failed retry after a prior success.


Describe how your implementation supports the operating context above, and include checks for the operational situations your design handles. Record assumptions about workload and shared operation, the expected behavior during interruptions, and the limits of the verification you performed.

# Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

# Execution plan — IT access requests

## Objective and scope

Build a runnable application that uses a language model to extract facts from exported messages, validates the results, and prepares an IT review queue. Support incremental inspection, overlapping operators, source updates, interruptions, retries, and traceable history. Approval remains a human decision.

This plan translates [CHALLENGE.md](../CHALLENGE.md), [requirements.md](requirements.md), [office-policy.md](../materials/office-policy.md), and [snapshot.schema.json](../snapshot.schema.json) into milestones. Those files remain authoritative. All milestones are pending; this document describes planned behavior, not observed results.

## Proposed architecture

Use Python 3.12, a CLI, SQLite, JSON Schema validation, and adapters for deterministic mock responses and a real model provider. Pin dependencies and commit a lockfile. Select and verify one provider, SDK, and model during milestone 1 before claiming support.

Support multiple CLI processes on one host with a local SQLite database. Use short transactions, a busy timeout, bounded worker concurrency, transactional job claims, expiring leases, and stale-worker fencing. Never hold a database transaction during a model call. Multi-host deployment and network-mounted SQLite are outside the initial scope.

Proposed structure:

```text
src/access_requests/
  cli.py              # Intake, queue, resume, retry, history, export, accuracy
  intake.py           # Input validation, hashing, scheduling
  storage.py          # Revisions, attempts, leases, current view, transactions
  providers/          # Real provider and mock adapters
  prompts/            # Versioned extraction instructions
  validation.py       # Completion, schema, quote, and date checks
  routing.py          # Ordered review-policy rules
  export.py           # Consistent deliverable snapshots
  accuracy.py         # Independent expected-vs-observed comparison
tests/fixtures/       # Mock responses and hand-authored expectations
deliverables/         # Required outputs and evidence
```

## Milestones

### 1. Establish the runtime and operator contract

- Add packaging, dependency lockfile, CLI entry point, and ignored local state/secret files.
- Choose and implement the real provider integration. Read the facilitator's credential from `API_KEY`; mock mode must require no key.
- Define and validate configuration for provider/model, endpoint if applicable, request timeout, maximum attempts, concurrency, rate limits, and database path.
- Document the supported runtime/provider/model and exact install, intake, queue, resume, retry, history, export, test, and accuracy commands.

**Completion criteria:** a clean environment installs locked dependencies, displays CLI help, runs a mock smoke test, and rejects missing live credentials without leaking secrets. Label live behavior as unverified until actually checked.

### 2. Build durable intake and source history

- Parse each UTF-8 JSON export independently and require a message string. Record malformed input as a document failure without stopping other work.
- Set `document_id` to the filename and `source_sha256` to the hash of original file bytes. Keep the message-stated request ID separate. Reject ambiguous duplicate filenames within a batch.
- Persist immutable source revisions, processing configurations, jobs, attempts, results, and a current pointer per document. Retain source bytes for reproducible retries.
- Fingerprint provider/model, prompt, schema, model request parameters, validation/routing implementation version, and policy content/version. Reuse successful results only when source and relevant configuration match. Refresh when either changes; keep failed attempts visible for explicit recovery.
- Prevent duplicate jobs across overlapping operators. Check source generations and leases on commit so an older or expired worker cannot overwrite newer work.
- Treat later batches as additions/updates; absence does not withdraw a document. Define latest source by persisted database intake order rather than export timestamp.

**Completion criteria:** unchanged reruns keep one current entry per document; updates retain history; omitted documents remain; overlapping intake is coherent; and a superseded attempt cannot replace the latest source.

### 3. Implement extraction and response validation

- Treat messages as untrusted data, including embedded instructions. Derive business facts only from `message`, never export timestamps or subjects.
- Request every schema field, exact supporting quotes, and issues for missing or uncertain facts. Preserve conflicts, honour explicit corrections, keep relative dates unresolved, and extract the new permission for change requests.
- Check provider completion status before using content. Explicitly handle refusal, truncation/interruption, malformed JSON, schema violations, timeout, rate limiting, and provider errors.
- Validate quotes as substrings of the decoded message and check calendar dates/date ordering. Document which failures invalidate extraction and which become clarification issues.
- Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient failures, respecting provider retry guidance. Record redacted errors and provider/model provenance per attempt.

**Completion criteria:** mock tests exercise all response paths; refused/interrupted/invalid responses never enter the queue as validated facts. Include a working real adapter and a redacted representative request even if recorded observations use mocks.

### 4. Implement routing and incremental queue inspection

Apply policy rules in this order after extraction validation:

| Condition | Status | Owner | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Instruction-override attempt | review | IT Service Desk | inspect-message |
| Withdrawal with request ID and date | review | IT Service Desk | confirm-withdrawal |
| Other/unknown kind, conflict, identifier mismatch, missing required fact, or reversed date range | needs-information | IT Service Desk | clarify |
| Complete new/change involving production, write, or admin | review | Security Review | review-risk-then-owner |
| Complete new/change staging/read | review | System Owner | review-request |
| Extraction failure | error | IT Service Desk | retry-extraction |

- Preserve attempted overrides as evidence and identify them in issues. Managers are contacts, not approvers.
- Expose completed results while other jobs run, with pending/running/failed counts and source/attempt identifiers. Keep job state separate from business review status.
- During refresh, identify newer pending work and label any older successful result with its earlier source and attempt. A failed refresh becomes the current error with null extraction; keep the previous success in history.
- Export queue and extraction records from one database read snapshot. Publish versioned export directories through one atomic manifest/pointer switch; materialize required submission paths from one completed generation.

**Completion criteria:** routing is deterministic and respects precedence; errors have actionable retry instructions; current queue and extraction records agree on document/source/attempt; readers can inspect results during processing and export without mixing generations.

### 5. Verify recovery and shared operation

- Persist jobs before model calls and commit each result independently. Resume unfinished work and reclaim expired leases after interruption, fencing stale workers from committing.
- Provide explicit retry and history commands. Configure bounded timeouts, retries, concurrency, rate limits, and lease renewal.
- Test stop/resume, two overlapping operators, slow messages, rate limits, unchanged reruns, changed source/configuration/policy, batch omission, stale-worker fencing, and consistent concurrent exports.
- Include required tests for a complete request, missing dates, conflicting facts, embedded instructions, provider failure, refusal/interruption, and a failed retry following success.
- Exercise all 20 inputs and a synthetic 2,000-message mock batch. Record measurements and limits; mock timings do not establish live provider throughput.

**Completion criteria:** completed work survives interruption; unfinished work resumes; one slow message leaves other results available; a failed retry is visible while history preserves success. Document single-host limits and the possibility of repeated provider calls after a crash; do not claim exactly-once remote execution.

### 6. Build independent accuracy checks

- Hand-author expected facts from all 20 messages and policy independently of extraction outputs. Add one new paraphrased request and expected facts. Store reference fixtures separately from actual results.
- Specify every schema field and routing expectation for all 21 cases. The anchors below guide coverage but are not the full reference dataset.
- Define exact-match counting before evaluation: compare the 13 scalar schema fields, including expected nulls, without hidden normalization. Report correct scalar cells / 273 expected cells (21 × 13). Missing/error records earn zero matching cells and remain in the denominator.
- Score supporting quotes, issues, and status/owner/next-action separately with documented criteria. Check quote containment and required evidence coverage. Report fabricated facts and unsupported assertions separately. Define expected business-purpose strings and disclose the limits of exact string scoring.

|---|---|

| IT-003 | Missing environment, permission, explicit dates → clarify |

# IT Access Request Intake

A planned application for Northstar Labs that turns free-text access requests into structured records and an IT review queue. It will use a language model to extract facts and the supplied office policy to identify the reviewer and next action. Approval remains a human decision.

**Current status: planning only.** This repository contains the challenge, requirements, policy, schema, and 20 fictional request exports. Application code, dependencies, tests, and generated deliverables have not been implemented.

The [execution plan](docs/execution-plan.md) defines the architecture, milestones, completion criteria, verification strategy, and submission checklist.

## Goals

- Extract explicit facts with exact source quotes; preserve missing/conflicting values as null with explanatory issues.
- Route requests to IT Service Desk, Security Review, or System Owner using the policy's ordered rules.
- Make completed results available while other messages are processing.
- Support overlapping operators, resumable intake, visible failures, and reproducible retries.
- Track source hashes, processing settings, revisions, and earlier attempts.
- Validate behavior against independent expectations for all 20 messages and one new paraphrase.

## Repository structure

```text
CHALLENGE.md               Assignment and submission requirements
README.md                  Project overview and implementation status
docs/
  requirements.md          Operating context and required behavior
  execution-plan.md        Implementation milestones and completion criteria
materials/
  office-policy.md         Extraction, routing, and recovery rules
  requests/                20 source-message JSON exports
snapshot.schema.json       Required extraction object schema
```

Read [CHALLENGE.md](CHALLENGE.md), the [requirements](docs/requirements.md), [office policy](materials/office-policy.md), and [schema](snapshot.schema.json) before implementing the plan.

## Proposed design

Use a Python 3.12 CLI with a local SQLite database, bounded concurrent workers, and mock and real provider adapters. Separate extraction, response validation, and deterministic policy routing. Persist each message independently so one slow or failed response leaves other results available.

The database will retain source revisions, configuration fingerprints, attempts, and history. Unchanged successful inputs will reuse results. Changed sources or relevant settings will trigger refreshes; failed refreshes will appear as current errors while earlier successes remain in history. Consistent snapshot exports will keep queue and extraction records aligned.

The initial shared-operation scope is multiple CLI processes on one host with a local database. Multi-host operation requires a different storage/deployment design. Verification will cover the samples and a synthetic 2,000-message mock batch.

## Setup and operator interface

There is no runnable application yet. Python 3.12 is proposed; the supported provider, model, SDK, dependencies, and install command will be pinned in the first milestone. The real integration must read credentials from `API_KEY`. Mock mode will require no key.

These commands define the **proposed interface** and are not available yet:

```sh
access-requests intake materials/requests --provider mock
access-requests queue
access-requests resume
access-requests retry --document-id IT-001.json
access-requests history --document-id IT-001.json
access-requests export --output deliverables
access-requests accuracy --expected tests/fixtures/expected.json --actual deliverables/extractions.jsonl
python -m pytest
```

`queue` will expose completed results and outstanding work during intake. `resume` will recover unfinished jobs; `retry` will create a traceable new attempt. Live intake will require a configured provider/model and `API_KEY`. Exact supported flags and additional environment-variable names will be documented after implementation and verification.

## Planned outputs and verification

Required outputs are `deliverables/extractions.jsonl`, `deliverables/queue.json`, `deliverables/accuracy.md`, `deliverables/request-evidence.json`, and `deliverables/verification.md`. Source code, a dependency lockfile, extraction instructions, model configuration, and coding-session capture are also required.

Automated checks will cover extraction edge cases, policy precedence, malformed/refused/interrupted responses, unchanged reruns, source/configuration changes, failed retries after success, concurrent operators, and interruption recovery. Accuracy expectations will come from messages and policy independently of extraction output. Mock and any live observations will be labelled separately. No accuracy or performance results have been measured yet.

## Next steps

1. Establish packaging, the provider/runtime contract, and CLI interface.
2. Implement durable intake, versioning, and transactional job claims.
3. Add extraction, validation, routing, queue inspection, and recovery.
4. Build accuracy fixtures, run verification, and generate deliverables.
5. Update this README with verified setup and exact commands, then complete the submission checklist.

See the [execution plan](docs/execution-plan.md) for completion criteria for each step.

## Objective and scope

Build a runnable application that uses a language model to extract facts from exported messages, validates the results, and prepares an IT review queue. This plan translates [CHALLENGE.md](../CHALLENGE.md), [requirements.md](requirements.md), [office-policy.md](../materials/office-policy.md), and [snapshot.schema.json](../snapshot.schema.json) into milestones. ## Proposed architecture

Use Python 3.12, a CLI, SQLite, JSON Schema validation, and adapters for deterministic mock responses and the OpenAI Responses API through the Python SDK. Pin dependencies and commit a lockfile. Verify account access and pin one model and SDK during milestone 1 before claiming support. The [README operator contract](../README.md#setup) defines the exact proposed setup, configuration names/defaults, and commands to implement and verify.

Support multiple CLI processes on one host with a local SQLite database. Use short transactions, a busy timeout, bounded worker concurrency, transactional job claims, expiring leases, and stale-worker fencing. Never hold a database transaction during a model call. # Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.
